detail.body:
## Purpose
We met a problem that adding `'draft_tensor_parallel_size': 1` or `'draft_tensor_parallel_size': 2` in server script, the draft model tensor parallel size is still same as the main model.
```
Qwen3ForCausalLM(
  (model): Qwen3Model(
    (embed_tokens): VocabParallelEmbedding(num_embeddings=18992, embedding_dim=5120, org_vocab_size=151936, num_embeddings_padded=151936, tp_size=8)
    (layers): ModuleList(
      (0-63): 64 x Qwen3DecoderLayer(
        (self_attn): Qwen3Attention(
          (qkv_proj): QKVParallelLinear(in_features=5120, output_features=1280, bias=False, tp_size=8, gather_output=False)
          (o_proj): RowParallelLinear(in_features=1024, output_features=5120, bias=False, tp_size=8, reduce_results=True)
          (rotary_emb): YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding(head_size=128, rotary_dim=128, max_position_embeddings=40960, base=1000000, is_neox_style=True)
          (attn): Attention(head_size=128, num_heads=8, num_kv_heads=1, scale=0.08838834764831845, backend=FlashAttentionImpl)
          (q_norm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=128, eps=1e-06)
          (k_norm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=128, eps=1e-06)
        )
        (mlp): Qwen2MLP(
          (gate_up_proj): MergedColumnParallelLinear(in_features=5120, output_features=6400, bias=False, tp_size=8, gather_output=False)
          (down_proj): RowParallelLinear(in_features=3200, output_features=5120, bias=False, tp_size=8, reduce_results=True)
          (act_fn): SiluAndMul()
        )
        (input_layernorm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=5120, eps=1e-06)
        (post_attention_layernorm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=5120, eps=1e-06)
      )
    )
    (norm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=5120, eps=1e-06)
  )
  (lm_head): ParallelLMHead(num_embeddings=18992, embedding_dim=5120, org_vocab_size=151936, num_embeddings_padded=151936, tp_size=8)
  (logits_processor): LogitsProcessor(vocab_size=151936, org_vocab_size=151936, scale=1.0, logits_as_input=False)
)

EagleQwen3ForCausalLM(
  (model): Qwen3Model(
    (embed_tokens): VocabParallelEmbedding(num_embeddings=18992, embedding_dim=5120, org_vocab_size=151936, num_embeddings_padded=151936, tp_size=8)
    (layers): ModuleList(
      (0): Qwen3EalgeDecoderLayer(
        (self_attn): Qwen3Attention(
          (qkv_proj): QKVParallelLinear(in_features=5120, output_features=1280, bias=False, tp_size=8, gather_output=False)
          (o_proj): RowParallelLinear(in_features=1024, output_features=5120, bias=False, tp_size=8, reduce_results=True)
          (rotary_emb): YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding(head_size=128, rotary_dim=128, max_position_embeddings=40960, base=1000000, is_neox_style=True)
          (attn): Attention(head_size=128, num_heads=8, num_kv_heads=1, scale=0.08838834764831845, backend=FlashAttentionImpl)
          (q_norm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=128, eps=1e-06)
          (k_norm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=128, eps=1e-06)
        )
        (mlp): Qwen3MLP(
          (gate_up_proj): MergedColumnParallelLinear(in_features=5120, output_features=6400, bias=False, tp_size=8, gather_output=False)
          (down_proj): RowParallelLinear(in_features=3200, output_features=5120, bias=False, tp_size=8, reduce_results=True)
          (act_fn): SiluAndMul()
        )
        (post_attention_layernorm): RMSNorm(hidden_size=5120, eps=1e-06)
        (input_layernorm): Identity()
      )
    )
    (fc): Linear(in_features=10240, out_features=5120, bias=False)
  )
  (lm_head): ParallelLMHead(num_embeddings=18992, embedding_dim=5120, org_vocab_size=151936, num_embeddings_padded=151936, tp_size=8)
  (logits_processor): LogitsProcessor(vocab_size=151936, org_vocab_size=151936, scale=1.0, logits_as_input=False)
)
```
Quick start script:
```
nohup python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --model=$model_path \
    --served-model-name auto \
    --host $host \
    --port $port \
    --tensor-parallel-size $tp \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --no-enforce-eager \
    --max-num-seqs 256  \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --speculative_config '{"model": "modelpath", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "method": "eagle3", "draft_tensor_parallel_size": 2}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [6,12,24],"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    > run.log &
```
The reason is that draft model shares same communication group with main model. We reuse function `patch_tensor_parallel_group` to deal with the problem.
Possibly related to issue #31345

## Test Plan
Test in server mode, print acceptance length to evaluate draft model accuracy with different tp size.

## Test Result
test in deepseek-v3 with self-data
```
(APIServer pid=79877) INFO 01-13 15:48:00 [metrics.py:100] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 3.20, Accepted throughput: 31.70 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 71.99 tokens/s, Accepted: 317 tokens, Drafted: 720 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.729, 0.549, 0.382, 0.312, 0.229, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 44.0%
```
test in qwen3-235b with self-data
```
(APIServer pid=85341) INFO 01-13 16:29:06 [metrics.py:100] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 4.12, Accepted throughput: 23.40 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 52.49 tokens/s, Accepted: 234 tokens, Drafted: 525 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.787, 0.653, 0.480, 0.387, 0.293, 0.293, 0.227, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 44.6%
```
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds end-to-end support for draft models using a different tensor-parallel (TP) size than the target model.
> 
> - Relax `SpeculativeConfig._verify_and_get_draft_tp` validation so `draft_tensor_parallel_size` is no longer restricted to `{1, target TP}`
> - In `GPUModelRunner`, initialize a dedicated draft TP process group and run drafter ops under `patch_tensor_parallel_group(...)` (for load, propose, dummy_run)
> - In `EagleProposer`:
>   - Store original `tp_group` and implement `_reshard_draft_tp_tensor(...)` that `all_gather`s shards and slices to match the draft TP partition
>   - When sharing `embed_tokens`/`lm_head`, if shapes differ, reshard target weights to the draft TP shard; otherwise reuse modules directly
>   - Minor import consolidation (`get_pp_group`, `get_tp_group`) and small logging adjustments
>

inline_comments.body:
![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

This new method has two issues:
1.  The `all_gather_into_tensor` call on line 1326 is incorrect. It should gather shards of the main model's weight (`src_tensor`) across the main model's tensor parallel group. However, this function is executed when the active TP group is patched to be the draft model's group. Using the default world group for `all_gather_into_tensor` is also incorrect if `TP_size < world_size`. This will lead to incorrect weights being loaded for the draft model.
2.  The `print` statement on line 1328 appears to be for debugging and should be removed.

A potential fix for the first issue is to obtain the main model's TP group before patching and pass it down to this function to be used explicitly in the `all_gather_into_tensor` call.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The logic for creating `group_ranks` for the draft model's tensor parallel group is incorrect for distributed setups involving data or pipeline parallelism. The `reshape(-1, 1, 1, 1, draft_tp_size)` hardcodes other parallelism dimensions to 1, which is not generally true.

Assuming that tensor parallel ranks are contiguous (the fastest changing dimension), a simpler and more robust approach would be to reshape the world ranks directly.

```suggestion
            group_ranks = torch.arange(world_size).reshape(-1, draft_tp_size).tolist()
```

### Resharding function can return None causing crash **Medium Severity** The `_reshard_draft_tp_tensor` function initializes `dst_tensor` to `None` and only sets it if a parameter containing `target_name` is found in the draft model. If no matching parameter exists, the function returns `None`. The callers at lines 1123 and 1180 then attempt `nn.Parameter(resharded_tensor, ...)` which will fail with a confusing error when `resharded_tensor` is `None`. This could happen if draft and target models have different parameter naming conventions for embeddings or lm_head.

Hi @stormchasingg,

We've been hitting exactly the issue this PR addresses on a 4× DGX Spark / GB10 cluster running GLM 5.2 (744B/40B MoE, GlmMoeDsa architecture) with MTP=3 via vLLM 0.23.1rc1.dev190 (TP=4). GLM 5.2's MTP head goes through vLLM's `deepseek_v4` MTP module, same code path the fix touches, even though the model itself isn't a DeepSeek model. When we set `draft_tensor_parallel_size: 1`, the field is silently orphaned, EagleProposer in V1 doesn't honor it and the MTP layer ends up running at the target's TP=4, which costs roughly one full all-reduce per speculative step and largely cancels out the MTP speedup. From what we've read of this PR and the underlying issue (#31345), the approach you took is the right shape for the fix.
  
We can apply this PR to our chthonic-based vLLM image, run it on the actual 4×GB10 cluster with GLM 5.2 + MTP=3 as the workload, and report measured before/after numbers (decode tok/s, MTP acceptance rates, GPU memory at TP=4 vs TP=1 for the draft). That's the test coverage the reviewer asks flagged as missing.
  
Is the PR still active? Happy to:
  - Just run validation and report results back (no PR changes from us)
  - Pick up the reviewer asks (`all_gather` communicator, parameterized
    reshape, type annotations) and push commits if you're not on it
  - Whatever shape of contribution is most useful
  
If you've moved on and would rather we open a fresh PR building on your approach (with attribution), that works too. Mostly want to make sure the work doesn't get lost to stale-bot.
  
Thanks for the work so far.

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for different tensor parallel sizes for the draft model in speculative decoding. The core idea of using a separate TP group for the draft model and patching it during drafter operations is sound. However, I've found two critical issues:
1. The initialization of the draft model's TP group in `gpu_model_runner.py` is incorrect for distributed setups with data or pipeline parallelism.
2. The weight resharding logic in `eagle.py` for shared embeddings and lm_head is flawed, as it performs an `all_gather` operation in the wrong process group context. This will lead to incorrect weights being loaded.
I've also pointed out a leftover debug print statement. Addressing these critical issues is necessary for the feature to work correctly in distributed environments.

I'm not sure if supporting a draft model parallelism other than replicating or the same TP as main model is something we want - what's the reason behind doing this?

cc @benchislett

Left some comments, but overall I'm fine with the feature if it's useful. 

Can you also make sure that it will work with DP (if it is supported in the first place) and/or EP without any problems?
